title: Moncada Barracks, Santiago de Cuba
summary: The Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba began as a Spanish colonial military camp authorised in 1859, and later housed the Cuban army's Maceo Regiment. On 26 July 1953 Fidel Castro led an unsuccessful assault on it that started his revolutionary movement. It became a school in 1960.

uncertainty.note: Construction was authorised 1 October 1859 and the works began 24 January 1860. A fire destroyed the complex in 1937 and a new barracks opened in 1944. End is the present: it is a school and museum.

where.historical_name: Campo Militar de la Reina (later Reina Mercedes, then Cuartel Moncada), Spanish and then Cuban army garrison, Santiago de Cuba

importance.justification: The target of the 1953 assault that began the Cuban Revolution; it gave the 26th of July Movement its name.
